17 18 # FRAI · Framework of Responsible Artificial Intelligence 19 20 ![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/frai) 21 ![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/frai) 22 23 24 FRAI is an open-source toolkit that helps teams launch AI features responsibly. It guides you through evidence gathering, scans your code, and assembles documentation you can hand to reviewers: implementation checklists, model cards, risk files, evaluation reports, and compliance-aware RAG indexes. The toolkit ships as two packages that work together: 25 26 - `frai` – the command-line app with ready-to-run workflows. 27 - `frai-core` – the reusable SDK that powers the CLI and any custom integrations. 28 29 ### Short Answer 30 - `frai-core` is the library/SDK. Use it when you are embedding FRAI capabilities into your own tools, servers, automations, or extensions. 31 - `frai` is the CLI. It wraps `frai-core` to deliver an end-user experience with no coding required. 32 33 ### Why Keep Both? 34 - Independent versioning and stability 35 - `frai-core` can evolve APIs for integrators without forcing a CLI release. 36 - `frai` can improve UX/commands without breaking programmatic users. 37 - Reuse across surfaces 38 - `frai-core` powers the CLI today and future VS Code/Chrome extensions, GitHub Actions, internal CLIs, services, or SDKs. 39 - Smaller, focused installs 40 - Operators install the CLI. 41 - Builders install only the core library they need. 42 43 ### When to Use Each 44 - Choose **`frai` (CLI)** when you want interactive prompts, one-command scans, RAG indexing, evaluation reports, or CI-friendly automation without writing code. 45 - Choose **`frai-core` (SDK)** when you want API access to FRAI capabilities from Node scripts, services, custom CLIs, extensions, or unusual I/O flows. 46 47 ### Concrete Examples 48 - CLI user: run `frai --scan` and `frai eval` in a repository to generate governance docs and audit reports. 49 - Library user: call `Documents.generateDocuments` from an internal portal to produce standardized docs, use `Scanners.scanCodebase` inside a GitHub Action, or embed `Rag.indexDocuments` inside a VS Code extension for grounded hints. 50 51 In short: CLI = product; Core = platform. They overlap in capability on purpose but target different audiences and distribution needs. 52 53 --- 54 55 ## Getting Started with the CLI 56 57 1. Install the published CLI: 58 ```bash 59 npm install -g frai 60 ``` 61 2. Configure your OpenAI API key (needed for AI-generated tips and evaluations): 62 ```bash 63 frai --setup 64 ``` 65 Keys can be stored per-project (`.env`) or globally (`~/.config/frai/config`). You can also provide a one-off key using `frai --key sk-...`. 66 3. Run the interactive workflow: 67 ```bash 68 frai 69 ``` 70 FRAI walks you through feature discovery, writes `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`, and optionally exports PDFs. 71 72 Generated artefacts live in your current working directory. Supplementary commands cover scanning, evaluation, RAG indexing, and fine-tuning governance. 73 74 --- 75 76 ## CLI Command Reference 77 78 | Command | Purpose | 79 |---------|---------| 80 | `frai [options]` | Interactive documentation workflow with backward-compatible shortcut flags. | 81 | `frai generate [options]` | Explicit interactive workflow command. | 82 | `frai scan [--ci] [--json]` | Scan the repository for AI/ML indicators. | 83 | `frai setup [--key ] [--global]` | Store an OpenAI API key locally or globally. | 84 | `frai config` | Show key configuration status. | 85 | `frai docs list` / `frai docs clean` / `frai docs export` | Manage generated documentation. | 86 | `frai rag index [options]` | Build a local compliance-aware vector index. | 87 | `frai eval --outputs [...]` | Run baseline evaluation metrics and write reports. | 88 | `frai finetune template` / `frai finetune validate ` | Create or validate fine-tuning governance plans. | 89 | `frai update` | Check npm for the latest CLI release. | 90 91 ### Default Command: `frai [options]` 92 Runs the interactive documentation flow. Optional flags add shortcuts: 93 - `--scan` – run code scanning before questions. 94 - `--ci` – exit after scanning when no AI indicators are detected. 95 - `--setup` – jump directly into key configuration. 96 - `--key ` / `--global` – provide a key and optionally persist it globally. 97 - `--list-docs` / `--clean` – list or remove generated docs. 98 - `--export-pdf` – convert generated markdown to PDFs (requires `markdown-pdf`). 99 - `--show-config` – display key storage status. 100 - `--update` – check npm for a newer CLI version. 101 102 ### `frai generate [options]` 103 Same workflow as the default command, but scoped to documentation only. Options mirror the defaults: `--scan`, `--ci`, `--key`, `--global`, `--export-pdf`, and `--show-config`. 104 105 ### `frai scan` 106 Scans the repository for AI-related libraries, functions, and files. Use `--ci` for non-interactive mode or `--json` to emit raw JSON. 107 108 ### `frai setup` 109 Guided API key storage. Supply `--key ` for headless use and `--global` to persist at `~/.config/frai/config`. 110 111 ### `frai config` 112 Prints whether local (`.env`) or global configuration holds an API key. 113 114 ### `frai docs` 115 Utilities for generated artefacts: 116 - `frai docs list` – list detected `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`. 117 - `frai docs clean` – delete generated docs. 118 - `frai docs export` – export docs to PDF via `markdown-pdf`. 119 120 ### `frai rag index [options]` 121 Create a lightweight JSON vector store for compliance policies. 122 - `--input ` – file or directory to index (defaults to cwd). 123 - `--output ` – target JSON file (defaults to `frai-index.json`). 124 - `--chunk-size ` – words per chunk (default 800). 125 - `--extensions ` – allowlisted extensions (default `.md,.markdown,.txt,.json,.yaml,.yml`). 126 127 ### `frai eval` 128 Generate evaluation reports for model outputs. 129 - `--outputs ` *(required)* – JSON file with model outputs. 130 - `--references ` – JSON file with reference answers. 131 - `--report ` – output location (`frai-eval-report.json` by default). 132 - `--format ` – output format (defaults to JSON). Markdown reports include human-readable summaries for review boards. 133 134 ### `frai finetune` 135 Fine-tuning governance helpers: 136 - `frai finetune template [--output ]` – write a governance template JSON (`frai-finetune-plan.json` by default). 137 - `frai finetune validate [--readiness]` – validate a plan and optionally print readiness checkpoints and summaries. 138 139 ### `frai update` 140 Check npm for the latest `frai` release and print upgrade instructions. 141 142 --- 143 144 ## Using `frai-core` (SDK) 145 146 Install from npm: 147 ```bash 148 pnpm add frai-core 149 ``` 150 151 `frai-core` exposes modular helpers that the CLI uses under the hood: 152 - `Questionnaire` – interactive question flows. 153 - `Documents` – generate checklists, model cards, and risk files. 154 - `Scanners` – static analysis for AI indicators. 155 - `Rag` – policy-grounded indexing utilities. 156 - `Eval` – baseline evaluation metrics and report writers. 157 - `Finetune` – governance templates, validation, and readiness scoring. 158 - `Config` & `Providers` – key management and LLM provider wiring. 159 160 Example: generate documentation programmatically. 161 162 ```ts 163 import fs from 'fs/promises'; 164 import inquirer from 'inquirer'; 165 import { Documents, Questionnaire, Scanners } from 'frai-core'; 166 167 const answers = await Questionnaire.runQuestionnaire({ 168 prompt: (questions) => inquirer.prompt(questions) 169 }); 170 171 const { checklist, modelCard, riskFile } = Documents.generateDocuments({ answers }); 172 const scan = Scanners.scanCodebase({ root: process.cwd() }); 173 const aiContext = Documents.buildContextForAITips(answers); 174 175 await fs.writeFile('checklist.md', checklist); 176 await fs.writeFile('model_card.md', modelCard); 177 await fs.writeFile('risk_file.md', riskFile); 178 await fs.writeFile('scan-summary.json', JSON.stringify(scan, null, 2)); 179 await fs.writeFile('ai-context.txt', aiContext); 180 ``` 181 182 Because `frai-core` is a regular ESM package, you can import only the modules you need and embed FRAI capabilities inside automation pipelines, CI jobs, or custom products. 183 184 --- 185 186 ## Local Development 187 188 Clone the repository and work from source: 189 ```bash 190 pnpm install 191 pnpm --filter frai run build 192 node packages/frai-cli/dist/index.js --help 193 ``` 194 195 During development you can install the CLI locally without publishing: 196 ```bash 197 pnpm install --global ./packages/frai-cli 198 # then 199 frai --setup 200 ``` 201 202 Store your OpenAI key by running the CLI setup flow or setting `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `.env`. 203 204 --- 205 206 ## Publishing (Maintainers) 207 208 FRAI ships as two npm packages and they must be published independently. 209 210 1. Bump versions in `packages/frai-core/package.json` and `packages/frai-cli/package.json`. Update the CLI dependency to match the published `frai-core` version (drop `workspace:*`). 211 2. Build the CLI: 212 ```bash 213 pnpm --filter frai run build 214 ``` 215 3. Publish `frai-core` first, then `frai`: 216 ```bash 217 cd packages/frai-core && npm publish 218 cd ../frai-cli && npm publish 219 ``` 220 4. Verify on npm: 221 ```bash 222 npm view frai versions --json 223 npm view frai-core versions --json 224 ``` 225 226 --- 227 228 ## Learn More 229 - Website: [frai.cc](https://frai.cc) 230 - NPM package: [frai](https://www.npmjs.com/package/frai) 231 - docs/ai_feature_backlog.md – roadmap for AI capabilities. 232 - docs/eval_harness_design.md – evaluation harness design notes. 233 - docs/architecture-target.md – monorepo architecture. 234 235 *Framework of Responsible Artificial Intelligence* 236

1	# Evaluation Harness Design Notes (Day 10)
2	
3	## Goals
4	- Provide a lightweight, dependency-free baseline evaluation pipeline developers can run locally.
5	- Standardise reporting so evaluation results feed into documentation, CI, and governance workflows.
6	- Prepare ground for future metric plug-ins and external provider integrations.
7	
8	## MVP Scope
9	- JSON loader for model outputs (`--outputs`) and optional references (`--references`).
10	- Default metrics:
11	  - Exact match (case-insensitive string comparison).
12	  - Toxicity keyword scan (simple lexical filter).
13	  - Length variance (difference between outputs and references).
14	- Report generation: structured JSON + Markdown summaries.
15	- CLI command `frai eval` wrapping the core harness.
16	
17	## Data Expectations
18	- Outputs/reference files should be JSON arrays. Each element may be a string or object containing `text`/`output` fields.
19	- Future work: support tabular CSV, scored datasets, multi-turn conversations.
20

It provides an intelligent assistant that can scan repositories, generate documentation, and answer questions about your AI features. 210 211 ### Getting Started 212 213 From the monorepo root: 214 ```bash 215 pnpm agent:frai "Scan the repository and summarize AI risks." 216 ``` 217 218 ### Interactive Mode 219 220 Launch a chat-style session: 221 ```bash 222 pnpm agent:frai --interactive --verbose 223 ``` 224 225 The agent supports two tools: 226 - **`scan_repository`** – Scans your codebase for AI indicators using FRAI's static detectors. 227 - **`generate_responsible_ai_docs`** – Generates `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md` from questionnaire answers. 228 229 ### Example Usage 230 231 Scan a repository: 232 ```bash 233 pnpm agent:frai "Scan the repo and tell me what AI-related code you found." 234 ``` 235 236 Generate documentation (with questionnaire answers): 237 ```bash 238 pnpm agent:frai "Generate the docs with these answers: { 239 \"core\": { \"name\": \"ReviewCopilot\", \"purpose\": \"assistant\" }, 240 \"impact\": { \"stakeholders\": [\"developers\"], \"impactLevel\": \"medium\" }, 241 \"data\": { \"sources\": [\"internal docs\"], \"retention\": \"30 days\" }, 242 \"performance\": { \"metrics\": [\"accuracy\"] }, 243 \"monitoring\": { \"strategy\": \"daily review\" }, 244 \"bias\": { \"mitigations\": [\"red teaming\"] } 245 }" 246 ``` 247 248 ### API Usage 249 250 ```ts 251 import { createFraIAgentExecutor } from "frai-agent"; 252 253 const executor = await createFraIAgentExecutor({ 254 model: "gpt-4o-mini", 255 verbose: true 256 }); 257 258 const result = await executor.invoke({ 259 input: "scan the repository", 260 chat_history: [] 261 }); 262 263 console.log(result.output); 264 ``` 265 266 `frai-agent` reuses FRAI's configuration system, so it automatically discovers your `OPENAI_API_KEY` from `.env` or global config. 267 268 --- 269 270 ## Responsible AI Gate (`frai gate`) 271 272 **The idea in one sentence: an AI feature spec is not done until seven responsible-AI questions are answered, and the gate blocks the build until they are.** 273 274 275 276 The seven checks: **risk tier** (EU AI Act-aligned; high-risk needs a named human sign-off) · **data & privacy** · **human oversight** · **evaluation thresholds** · **bias & fairness** · **monitoring & rollback** · **transparency & incidents**. Verdicts: ✅ PASS · ⚠️ WARN · ⛔ BLOCK (exit 1). 277 278 ### Add it to any app in 60 seconds 279 280 Works in any repo - new app, existing app, any language: 281 282 ```bash 283 npx frai-gate init --ci 284 ``` 285 286 That drops `FRAI-SPEC.md` (a spec template with the gate built in) and a GitHub Action that runs the gate on every PR. Answer the gate, then: 287 288 ```bash 289 npx frai-gate check FRAI-SPEC.md 290 ``` 291 292 No API key needed for the check. Two smarter commands use a read-only agent (Claude Code auth or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`): 293 294 ```bash 295 npx frai-gate draft # scans YOUR code and drafts the gate answers from it, 296 # with file:line citations and NEEDS HUMAN INPUT markers 297 npx frai-gate check FRAI-SPEC.md --smart # adversarial review: catches vague answers and 298 # spec claims your code contradicts 299 ``` 300 301 ### If you build with AI coding agents 302 303 ```bash 304 npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai-skills 305 ``` 306 307 installs the `responsible-ai-spec` skill: every spec your agent writes includes the gate, and the agent is forbidden from self-approving high-risk features - a named human signs. Claude Code users in this repo also get `/rai-spec`. 308 309 Everything is also available as `frai gate ...` inside the main CLI, and programmatically via `import { validateSpec } from 'frai-gate'`. Worked example (the one from the demo video): [`examples/support-triage-demo/`](examples/support-triage-demo). Design notes: `docs/rai-gate-design.md`. 310 311 --- 312 313 ## Local Development 314 315 Clone the repository and work from source: 316 ```bash 317 pnpm install 318 pnpm --filter frai run build 319 node packages/frai-cli/dist/index.js --help 320 ``` 321 322 During development you can install the CLI locally without publishing: 323 ```bash 324 pnpm install --global ./packages/frai-cli 325 # then 326 frai --setup 327 ``` 328 329 Store your OpenAI key by running the CLI setup flow or setting `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `.env`. 330 331 --- 332 333 ## Publishing (Maintainers) 334 335 FRAI ships as two npm packages and they must be published independently. 336 337 1. Bump versions in `packages/frai-core/package.json` and `packages/frai-cli/package.json`. Update the CLI dependency to match the published `frai-core` version (drop `workspace:*`). 338 2. Build the CLI: 339 ```bash 340 pnpm --filter frai run build 341 ``` 342 3. Publish `frai-core` first, then `frai`: 343 ```bash 344 cd packages/frai-core && npm publish 345 cd ../frai-cli && npm publish 346 ``` 347 4. Verify on npm: 348 ```bash 349 npm view frai versions --json 350 npm view frai-core versions --json 351 ``` 352 353 --- 354 355 ## Learn More 356 - Website: [frai.cc](https://frai.cc) 357 - NPM package: [frai](https://www.npmjs.com/package/frai) 358 - docs/ai_feature_backlog.md – roadmap for AI capabilities. 359 - docs/eval_harness_design.md – evaluation harness design notes. 360 - docs/architecture-target.md – monorepo architecture. 361 362 *Framework of Responsible Artificial Intelligence* 363

1	# FRAI Open Source Roadmap
2	
3	## Overview
4	- Mission: deliver a modular, contribution-friendly responsible AI toolkit spanning CLI, SDKs, guardrails, RAG workflows, and evaluation pipelines.
5	- Strategy: refactor the existing `frai` package into a monorepo of reusable modules, layer advanced AI/ML/NLP capabilities, and ship polished developer tooling (CLI, SDKs, VS Code extension, Docker images).
6	- Boundary: keep core compliance workflows open source while allowing optional hand-offs to the commercial FRAI SaaS.
7	
8	## Guiding Engineering Principles
9	- Favour small, composable modules with clear contracts (SOLID, clean architecture).
10	- Maintain full test coverage for new logic; TDD for critical scanners and generators.
11	- Ship with observable metrics and telemetry opt-in to validate user value.
12	- Bias toward DX excellence (typed APIs, docs, examples) to reduce integration friction.
13	- Prioritise AI features that solve concrete governance, audit, and safety pain points for practitioners.
14	
15	## Day-by-Day Plan (First 14 Days)
16	
17	### Week 1 – Restructure & Baseline
18	- ✅ **Day 1:** Run repository inventory, document current architecture, capture CLI behaviour; store findings in `docs/analysis.md`.
19	- ✅ **Day 2:** Finalise target monorepo design, module contracts, and dependency graph; draft `docs/architecture-target.md`.
20	- ✅ **Day 3:** Initialize pnpm/Turborepo workspace, scaffold `packages/frai-core` & `packages/frai-cli`, configure shared lint/test setup.
21	- ✅ **Day 4:** Port configuration & environment handling into `frai-core` modules; create unit tests for config loaders.
22	- ✅ **Day 5:** Migrate questionnaire logic and answer validation into `frai-core`; add Jest/Vitest coverage for prompt flows.
23	- ✅ **Day 6:** Extract document generators/templates, implement override mechanism, and add snapshot tests.
24	- ✅ **Day 7:** Build modular scanning engine with pluggable detectors; run integration tests using `examples/` fixtures.
25	
26	### Week 2 – AI Feature Foundations & Tooling
27	- ✅ **Day 8:** Assemble AI feature backlog with user stories; prioritise RAG, eval, fine-tuning governance; publish roadmap entries.
28	- ✅ **Day 9:** Implement `frai rag index` command, vector store abstraction, and RAG helper modules; cover with CLI tests.
29	- ✅ **Day 10:** Scaffold `frai eval` baseline metrics leveraging open-source models; ensure configurable thresholds and reporting.
30	- ✅ **Day 11:** Implement AI provider abstraction (`frai-core/src/providers`) supporting OpenAI + future adapters with comprehensive test coverage.
31	- ✅ **Day 12:** Draft fine-tuning governance spec (dataset audit, training hooks, bias evals); prototype config schema.
32	- **Day 13:** Develop VS Code MCP endpoint + extension scaffold reading data from `frai-core`; document protocol usage.
33	- **Day 14:** Author problem-solution playbooks (RAG compliance, LLM agent docs) in `/docs`; tie features to user pain points.
34	- **Day 15:** Add opt-in telemetry, gather KPIs (usage of new commands/tests), and produce sprint retrospective summary.
35	
36	## Workstreams (Weeks 3-6)
37	
38	### 1. Clean Architecture & Repo Structure (Weeks 0-2)
39	- Stand up pnpm/Turborepo monorepo with `packages/frai-cli` + `packages/frai-core`; migrate logic from `frai.mjs` into modular `/src` files.
40	- Add ESLint, Prettier, Vitest/Jest, and GitHub Actions for lint + test + coverage enforcement.
41	- Expose typed interfaces (TypeScript declarations or JSDoc) for generators, scanners, and template APIs.
42	- Publish `v1.2.0-alpha` showcasing the refactor; update README + CHANGELOG accordingly.
43	
44	### 2. AI/ML/NLP Feature Foundations (Weeks 2-4)
45	- Modular scanner engine supporting multi-language detectors and pluggable NLP rule packs.
46	- Launch `frai-rag` helpers for policy/document vectorization and CLI command `frai rag index`.
47	- Implement `frai eval` baseline metrics (bias/toxicity) with extensible hooks; document sample configs.
48	- Design fine-tuning governance toolkit covering dataset audits, training hooks, and post-tuning checks.
49	
50	### 3. Developer Experience & Distribution (Weeks 4-6)
51	- Release `frai-vscode` extension MVP with MCP integration, live checklists, and scan results.
52	- Package Docker images (`frai/cli`, `frai/eval`) and umbrella installers (`npx frai setup`, `pip install frai-suite`).
53	- Publish contributor guidelines, code of conduct, and Phase 1 roadmap issues to invite community participation.
54	
55	## Feature Roadmap Highlights
56	- **frai-guard:** runtime guardrails for LLM responses (jailbreak detection, toxicity filters, provenance logging).
57	- **frai-rag:** compliance-aware RAG toolkit integrating LangChain/LangGraph, vector stores, and policy prompts.
58	- **frai-eval:** evaluation harness with reproducible notebooks, MCP endpoints, and regression dashboards.
59	- **frai-finetune:** responsible fine-tuning pipelines integrating dataset audits and post-hoc bias testing.
60	- **frai-templates & connectors:** starter apps, CI recipes, and marketplace for community scanners (`frai-plugin-*`).
61	
62	## Packaging & Distribution
63	- npm: `frai`, `frai-cli`, `frai-core`, `frai-sdk-js`, guard/connector plugins.
64	- PyPI: `frai-sdk`, `frai-guard`, future evaluation/finetune helpers.
65	- IDE: VS Code marketplace (`frai-vscode`) and MCP packages for agentic IDE copilots.
66	- Containers: `frai/cli`, `frai/eval`, `frai/rag` images for CI/CD environments.
67	- Documentation: `docs/` site (Docusaurus/Mintlify) with tutorials, API references, and governance guides.
68	
69	## Audience & Adoption Paths
70	- **Startup AI teams:** run `frai init`, integrate GitHub Action gates, iterate with VS Code extension.
71	- **Enterprise governance offices:** operate Dockerized checks, manage policy repositories, audit fine-tuning workflows.
72	- **Applied ML engineers:** embed SDKs in training pipelines, run `frai eval`, leverage MCP hints while developing.
73	- **Agentic workflow builders:** wire `frai-guard` and `frai-rag` into LangChain/LangGraph with MCP orchestration.
74	- **Partners & solution architects:** customize templates, publish connectors, deliver compliant proof-of-concepts.
75	- **Researchers & community contributors:** explore labs datasets, author new guardrails, and engage via RFCs.
76	
77	## Next Actions
78	1. Create GitHub project board reflecting day-by-day tasks and broader workstreams; assign owners.
79	2. Complete repo analysis (Day 1/2 goals) and publish architecture blueprint in `docs/analysis.md`.
80	3. Execute monorepo migration (Days 3-7) with lint/test automation and alpha release.
81	4. Deliver AI feature prototypes (Days 8-14) focusing on concrete user problems documented in playbooks.
82	5. Schedule release cadence aligning npm, PyPI, VS Code, Docker, and MCP outputs; publish compatibility matrix.

1	# Evaluation Harness Design Notes (Day 10)
2	
3	## Goals
4	- Provide a lightweight, dependency-free baseline evaluation pipeline developers can run locally.
5	- Standardise reporting so evaluation results feed into documentation, CI, and governance workflows.
6	- Prepare ground for future metric plug-ins and external provider integrations.
7	
8	## MVP Scope
9	- JSON loader for model outputs (`--outputs`) and optional references (`--references`).
10	- Default metrics:
11	  - Exact match (case-insensitive string comparison).
12	  - Toxicity keyword scan (simple lexical filter).
13	  - Length variance (difference between outputs and references).
14	- Report generation: structured JSON + Markdown summaries.
15	- CLI command `frai eval` wrapping the core harness.
16	
17	## Data Expectations
18	- Outputs/reference files should be JSON arrays. Each element may be a string or object containing `text`/`output` fields.
19	- Future work: support tabular CSV, scored datasets, multi-turn conversations.
20	
21	## Extensibility Hooks
22	- `frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js` exposes `DEFAULT_METRICS`; additional metrics can be registered by passing custom evaluators to `runEvaluations`.
23	- `writeReport` accepts `format` argument to enable additional exporters (HTML, CSV) later.
24	- CLI parsing accommodates further evaluation subcommands (e.g., `frai eval bias`).

2	
3	## Objectives
4	- Prioritise high-impact AI/ML capabilities that align with FRAI's responsible AI mission.

8	## User Stories & Priorities
9	
10	### 1. Compliance-Aware RAG Toolkit (frai-rag)
11	- **User Story:** As an applied ML engineer building RAG pipelines, I want FRAI to help me index compliance artefacts and surface policy snippets so my answers remain compliant.
12	- **Problems Solved:** Lack of consistent governance context in retrieval layers; difficulty triaging policy requirements.
13	- **MVP Scope:**
14	  - CLI command `frai rag index` to ingest policy/docs into vector stores (Pinecone, pgvector, Weaviate).
15	  - Core APIs to embed FRAI docs and provide prompt templates with compliance guardrails.
16	  - SDK hooks (JS/Python) for querying compliance-aware context.
17	- **Dependencies:** frai-core embeddings driver, vector store config, CLI command wiring.
18	- **Priority:** P0 (kick off in upcoming days).
19	
20	### 2. Evaluation Harness (frai-eval)
21	- **User Story:** As a governance lead, I need automated bias/toxicity checks and regression tracking for models so I can sign off releases confidently.
22	- **Problems Solved:** Manual, ad-hoc evaluations; no regression history.
23	- **MVP Scope:**
24	  - CLI command `frai eval` with baseline metrics (bias, toxicity, hallucination).
25	  - Integration with open-source classifiers (Detoxify, Perspective API alternative, Fairlearn) with provider abstraction.
26	  - Exportable reports (JSON + Markdown) and hooks for CI.
27	- **Dependencies:** AI provider adapter layer, dataset fixtures, reporting templates.
28	- **Priority:** P0.
29	
30	### 3. Fine-Tuning Governance Toolkit (frai-finetune)
31	- **User Story:** As an ML platform owner, I want guardrails for dataset audits, hyperparameter tracking, and post-finetune evaluations to ensure responsible releases.
32	- **Problems Solved:** No governance trail for finetuned models; inconsistent audits.
33	- **MVP Scope:**
34	  - Config schema for dataset provenance and approval workflows.
35	  - CLI flow to generate checklist/model card deltas for finetuned models.
36	  - Integration with evaluation harness to run post-finetune tests automatically.
37	- **Dependencies:** Evaluation harness, configuration module, doc generation upgrades.
38	- **Priority:** P1 (start design, implementation after RAG/eval).
39	
40	### 4. MCP Integration Playbook
41	- **User Story:** As a developer using IDE copilots, I need FRAI to expose compliance checks via MCP so guardrails surface directly in my workflow.
42	- **Problems Solved:** Compliance context is disconnected from developer tools.
43	- **MVP Scope:**
44	  - MCP server wrapping frai-core scanner and questionnaire outputs.
45	  - VS Code extension commands calling MCP endpoints.
46	  - Documentation on registering FRAI MCP provider with third-party copilots.
47	- **Dependencies:** RAG/eval outputs, CLI commands, IDE packaging.
48	- **Priority:** P2 (design in parallel, implementation after core feature rollouts).
49	
50	### 5. AI Risk Simulation Engine
51	- **User Story:** As a risk officer, I want to simulate impact scenarios based on FRAI policies so I can prioritise mitigations.
52	- **Problems Solved:** No quantitative view of policy impact and risk trade-offs.

54	  - Scenario engine consuming policy configs and generating risk scores.

58	- **Priority:** P3 (longer-term backlog).

## FRAI-Core Structure and SDK Analysis

### 1. Directory Structure

The frai-core SDK is located at `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d11/with/h2-eval-thresholds/r3/packages/frai-core/` with the following modular structure:

```
frai-core/src/
├── index.js                     # Main entry point
├── config/                      # API key and config management
├── documents/                   # Documentation generation (checklist, model card, risk file)
├── eval/                        # Evaluation harness (main focus)
│   ├── index.js                # runEvaluations, loadDataset, generateReport, writeReport
│   ├── metrics.js              # Built-in metrics (exactMatch, toxicity, lengthVariance)
│   ├── reporters.js            # JSON/Markdown report formatters
│   └── index.test.js           # Test coverage
├── finetune/                    # Fine-tuning governance templates and validation
├── providers/                   # LLM provider abstraction (currently OpenAI)
├── questionnaire/               # Interactive question flows
├── rag/                         # RAG indexing and vector store utilities
└── scanners/                    # Static code analysis for AI/ML indicators
```

### 2. Main SDK Exports

The main entry point (`src/index.js`) re-exports all modules as namespaced exports:

```javascript
export * as Config from './config/index.js';
export * as Questionnaire from './questionnaire/index.js';
export * as Documents from './documents/index.js';
export * as Scanners from './scanners/index.js';
export * as Rag from './rag/index.js';
export * as Eval from './eval/index.js';
export * as Providers from './providers/index.js';
export * as Finetune from './finetune/index.js';
```

**Package.json configuration:**
- Main entry: `src/index.js`
- Type: ES Module (`"type": "module"`)
- Exports field: `".": "./src/index.js"`

### 3. The `runEvaluations` Function

**Location:** `/packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js` (lines 41-60)

**Function Signature:**
```javascript
export function runEvaluations({
  outputs,
  references,
  metrics = DEFAULT_METRICS
} = {})
```

**How it Works:**
1. Normalizes inputs to arrays (empty arrays if undefined)
2. Iterates through the metrics array
3. For each metric, it supports two calling patterns:
   - **Function metric:** `typeof metric === 'function'` → calls `metric(outputs, references)`
   - **Object metric:** `metric.evaluate === 'function'` → calls `metric.evaluate(outputs, references)`
4. Returns an array of evaluation result objects

**Error Handling:**
Throws `Error('Invalid metric supplied to runEvaluations.')` if metric is neither a function nor an object with an `evaluate` method.

### 4. How Custom Metrics Are Passed and Stored

**Custom Metric Interface:**

Users can pass custom metrics in two forms:

**Form 1: As a function**
```javascript
const myMetric = (outputs, references) => ({
  id: 'my_metric',
  label: 'My Custom Metric',
  score: 0.95,
  total: outputs.length,
  // ... additional fields
});
```

**Form 2: As an object with evaluate method**
```javascript
const myMetric = {
  evaluate: (outputs, references) => ({
    id: 'my_metric',
    label: 'My Custom Metric',
    score: 0.95,
    total: outputs.length
  })
};
```

**Expected Metric Result Format:**

Built-in metrics (`exactMatchMetric`, `toxicityMetric`, `lengthVarianceMetric`) show the standard structure:
```javascript
{
  id: string,              // Unique identifier (exact_match, toxicity, length_variance)
  label: string,           // Human-readable label
  score: number | null,    // Normalized 0-1 score, null for error cases
  total: number,           // Number of samples evaluated
  // ... metric-specific fields (matches, flagged, averageDelta, etc.)
}
```

**Passing custom metrics to runEvaluations:**
```javascript
const evaluations = Eval.runEvaluations({
  outputs: ['Hello', 'World'],
  references: ['hello', 'world'],
  metrics: [customMetric1, customMetric2]  // or mix with DEFAULT_METRICS
});
```

### 5. Built-in Metrics (in `src/eval/metrics.js`)

**DEFAULT_METRICS Array:**
```javascript
export const DEFAULT_METRICS = [
  exactMatchMetric,
  toxicityMetric,
  lengthVarianceMetric
];
```

**exactMatchMetric(outputs, references):**
- Case-insensitive string comparison
- Returns: score (0-1), total samples, match count, per-sample details

**toxicityMetric(outputs, bannedTerms = defaultBannedTerms):**
- Keyword-based lexical filter with default banned terms: 'hate', 'kill', 'violence', 'terrorist', 'racist', 'sexist'
- Returns: score (safety ratio), total samples, flagged count, flagged samples with terms

**lengthVarianceMetric(outputs, references):**
- Measures output length deviation from reference length
- Uses formula: `max(0, 1 - averageDelta / 500)`
- Returns: score (0-1), total samples, average delta (chars), per-sample deltas

### 6. Full SDK Usage Pattern

**Complete Example from frai-cli (lines 476-497):**

```javascript
import { Eval } from 'frai-core';

// Step 1: Load dataset
const dataset = Eval.loadDataset({
  outputsPath: options.outputs,
  referencesPath: options.references  // optional
});

// Step 2: Run evaluations with optional custom metrics
const evaluations = Eval.runEvaluations({
  outputs: dataset.outputs,
  references: dataset.references,
  metrics: DEFAULT_METRICS  // or custom metrics array
});

// Step 3: Generate report structure
const report = Eval.generateReport({
  evaluations,
  outputsPath: dataset.outputsPath,
  referencesPath: dataset.referencesPath,
  generatedAt: new Date().toISOString()
});

// Step 4: Write report to file
const resolvedPath = Eval.writeReport({
  report,
  format: 'json',  // or 'markdown'
  reportPath: './frai-eval-report.json'
});
```

### 7. Report Generation and Writing

**generateReport():**
- Aggregates evaluation results
- Extracts metadata (paths, timestamp, total samples)
- Returns structured report object

**writeReport():**
- Supports two formats: 'json' and 'markdown'
- JSON: Pretty-printed with 2-space indentation
- Markdown: Human-readable summary with metrics details
- Returns the resolved file path

### 8. Key Design Patterns

**Extensibility Hooks:**
1. Users can inject custom metrics via the `metrics` parameter
2. Report formatters can be extended (JSON/Markdown provided, HTML/CSV noted as future)
3. Dataset loader supports schema mapping (noted in design doc as future work)
4. Results pipe into documentation generators for risk files

**Current Limitations:**
- Custom metrics must follow the standard result object format
- No built-in threshold enforcement (scores are generated but not validated against thresholds)
- No integration between evaluation scores and gate checks (though gate schema expects numbers in evaluation section)
- No custom metric registration/plugin system at module level

This structure provides a solid foundation for SDK users to embed evaluation capabilities while maintaining flexibility for custom metrics and future extensions.

# Plan: Add `--threshold` option to `frai eval` for CI gating

## Context

Today `frai eval` always exits with code 0, making it impossible to gate CI pipelines on evaluation metric scores. This feature adds optional threshold checking to both the CLI and SDK, allowing users to fail the evaluation if metrics don't meet minimum standards.

**Example usage**: `frai eval --outputs outputs.json --threshold exact_match=0.9 --threshold toxicity=0.98`

This enables CI pipelines to block merges when model outputs don't meet quality thresholds.

---

## Implementation Overview

The feature adds threshold validation at three points:
1. **CLI argument parsing** – Parse and validate `--threshold` options (exit code 2 for malformed input)
2. **Core logic** – Add threshold checking to `generateReport` in frai-core
3. **Report output** – Include threshold results in JSON and Markdown reports

No changes to `runEvaluations` needed; the threshold logic applies at the reporting stage after metrics are computed.

---

## Phase 1: CLI Changes

### File: `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts`

**Changes to `frai eval` command definition (around line 708-717):**
- Add `.option('--threshold <metric>=<min>', 'Set minimum threshold for a metric (can be used multiple times)')` with `action` to collect into array
- Parse and validate thresholds before calling `runEvalCommand`

**New function: `parseAndValidateThresholds(thresholdStrings: string[])`**
- Input: array of strings like `["exact_match=0.9", "toxicity=0.98"]`
- For each string:
  - Split on `=` → must have exactly 2 parts
  - Validate metric exists in DEFAULT_METRICS (or is a known metric id)
  - Validate min is a valid number between 0 and 1
  - Return structured object: `{ [metricId]: minValue }` (e.g., `{ exact_match: 0.9, toxicity: 0.98 }`)
- On error: print usage message listing valid metric ids and exit 2 (do not write report)

**Changes to `runEvalCommand` (around line 476-497):**
- Parse thresholds (exit 2 on error)
- Pass `thresholds` object to `Eval.generateReport()`
- Check report's `passed` field after generation
- Exit 1 if `passed === false`, otherwise exit 0
- Write report regardless (success or failure)

---

## Phase 2: Core Logic Changes (frai-core)

### File: `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js`

**Update `generateReport` function signature (line 62):**
```javascript
export function generateReport({
  evaluations,
  outputsPath,
  referencesPath,
  thresholds = {},  // NEW: optional threshold object
  generatedAt = new Date().toISOString()
```

1. **CLI argument parsing** – Parse and validate `--threshold` options (exit code 2 for malformed input)

# Plan: Add `--threshold` option to `frai eval` for CI gating

## Context

Today `frai eval` always exits with code 0, making it impossible to gate CI pipelines on evaluation metric scores. This feature adds optional threshold checking to both the CLI and SDK, allowing users to fail the evaluation if metrics don't meet minimum standards.

**Example usage**: `frai eval --outputs outputs.json --threshold exact_match=0.9 --threshold toxicity=0.98`

This enables CI pipelines to block merges when model outputs don't meet quality thresholds.

---

## Implementation Overview

The feature adds threshold validation at three points:
1. **CLI argument parsing** – Parse and validate `--threshold` options (exit code 2 for malformed input)
2. **Core logic** – Add threshold checking to `generateReport` in frai-core
3. **Report output** – Include threshold results in JSON and Markdown reports

No changes to `runEvaluations` needed; the threshold logic applies at the reporting stage after metrics are computed.

---

## Phase 1: CLI Changes

### File: `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts`

**Update `EvalOptions` interface (line 51-56):**
```typescript
interface EvalOptions {
  outputs: string;
  references?: string;
  report?: string;
  format?: 'json' | 'markdown';
  threshold?: string[];  // NEW: collected from multiple --threshold options
}
```

**Changes to `frai eval` command definition (line 708-717):**
- Add `.option('--threshold <metric>=<min>', 'Set minimum threshold for a metric (can be used multiple times)')`
- Use Commander's built-in option value accumulation (each `--threshold` appends to an array)

**New function: `parseAndValidateThresholds(thresholdStrings: string[])`**
- Input: array of strings like `["exact_match=0.9", "toxicity=0.98"]`
- For each string:
  - Split on `=` → must have exactly 2 parts
  - Validate metric exists in DEFAULT_METRICS by id
  - Validate min is a valid number between 0 and 1
  - Return structured object: `{ [metricId]: minValue }` (e.g., `{ exact_match: 0.9, toxicity: 0.98 }`)
- On error: print usage message listing valid metric ids and exit 2 (do not write report)

**Changes to `runEvalCommand` (line 476-497):**
- Parse thresholds from `options.threshold` array (exit 2 on error)
- Pass `thresholds` object to `Eval.generateReport()`
- Check report's `passed` field after generation
- Exit 1 if `passed === false`, otherwise exit 0 (success)
- Write report regardless (success or failure) via `Eval.writeReport()`

---

## Phase 2: Core Logic Changes (frai-core)

### File: `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js`

**Current structure** (line 62-82): Report has `metadata` and `metrics` fields.

**Update `generateReport` function signature (line 62-67):**
```javascript
export function generateReport({
  evaluations,
  outputsPath,
  referencesPath,
  thresholds = {},  // NEW: optional threshold object
  generatedAt = new Date().toISOString()
})
```

**New logic inside `generateReport` (after building report):**
1. If `thresholds` is empty object:
   - Omit `passed` and `thresholds` fields (backward compatible)
2. If `thresholds` is provided:
   - Initialize `report.thresholds = []`
   - For each threshold entry `{ metric_id: minValue }`:
     - Find corresponding metric in `evaluations` by `id` match
     - Extract metric's `score` (or null if missing)
     - Determine result: `score !== null && score >= minValue` → `passed: true`, else `passed: false`
     - Push `{ metric, min, score, passed }` to `report.thresholds`
   - Set `report.passed = true` only if ALL thresholds passed (no false values in array)

**Data structure added to report:**
```javascript
{
  metadata: { ... },
  metrics: [ ... ],
  passed: boolean,  // NEW: true if all thresholds pass (or no thresholds)
  thresholds: [     // NEW: list of threshold results
    { metric: 'exact_match', min: 0.9, score: 0.85, passed: false },
    { metric: 'toxicity', min: 0.98, score: 0.99, passed: true }
  ]
}
```

**Backward compatibility:** When no thresholds provided, report structure is unchanged (no `passed` or `thresholds` fields).

---

## Phase 3: Report Formatting Updates

### File: `packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js`

**Update `toJson` function:**
- Already passes through all top-level report fields, so `passed` and `thresholds` will be included automatically via `JSON.stringify`
- No explicit changes needed; this is automatic

**Update `toMarkdown` function (line ~40+):**
- After metrics section, add new "Thresholds" section (if `report.thresholds` is non-empty):
  ```
  ## Thresholds
  
  - Exact Match: PASS (0.85 ≥ 0.9) ✓
  - Toxicity: FAIL (0.99 < 0.98) ✗
  ```
- Order: PASS entries first, then FAIL entries

**Edge case:** If no thresholds were specified, omit this section from both formats.

---

## Phase 4: Validation and Error Handling

**Valid metric ids** (from DEFAULT_METRICS in metrics.js):
- `exact_match` (id from exactMatchMetric)
- `toxicity` (id from toxicityMetric)
- `length_variance` (id from lengthVarianceMetric)
- Any custom metrics passed by SDK users

**Error cases (exit code 2):**
1. Malformed threshold string (not `<metric>=<number>`)
2. Minimum outside 0–1 range
3. Unknown metric id

**Error message format:**
```
Error: Invalid threshold 'exact_match=foo': minimum must be a number between 0 and 1.
Valid metrics: exact_match, toxicity, length_variance
```

**Metric with no score:**
- If metric exists but `score === null`, threshold fails (does not crash)
- Example: exact_match has no score when references are missing → threshold fails

---

## Phase 5: SDK Documentation

Update docstring for `generateReport` in `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js`:
```javascript
/**
 * generateReport - Aggregate evaluation results into a report object
 * @param {Object} evaluations - Array of metric results from runEvaluations
 * @param {string} outputsPath - Path to outputs file
 * @param {string} referencesPath - Path to references file (optional)
 * @param {Object} thresholds - Optional thresholds object { metricId: minScore }
 *                               e.g., { exact_match: 0.9, toxicity: 0.95 }
 * @returns {Object} Report with metrics, metadata, and optional passed/thresholds fields
 */
```

---

## Critical Files to Modify

| File | Changes | Impact |
|------|---------|--------|
| `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` | Add `--threshold` option, parsing, validation, exit codes | CLI behavior |
| `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js` | Add `thresholds` parameter to `generateReport`, compute `passed` and `thresholds` fields | Core logic, SDK |
| `packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js` | Add "Thresholds" section to markdown output | Report formatting |

---

## Backward Compatibility

- Without `--threshold` on CLI, behavior is identical (always exit 0)
- Without `thresholds` parameter in SDK, `generateReport` behaves identically
- Existing reports will gain `passed: true` and `thresholds: []` when thresholds are used, but this is additive

---

## Testing Plan

2. Multiple thresholds: both must pass for exit 0

5. Out-of-range threshold: `--threshold exact_match=1.5` → exit 2 with error message

1. `generateReport` with custom metrics and thresholds
2. Threshold validation for custom metrics works identically

---

- Use `process.exit(2)` for usage errors to match Node.js CLI conventions
- Threshold parsing is strict: whitespace in `metric=min` must be exact
- Metric id matching is case-sensitive (follow existing metric id naming)
- Reuse existing error logging patterns in `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts`

# Evaluation Harness Design Notes (Day 10)

## Goals
- Provide a lightweight, dependency-free baseline evaluation pipeline developers can run locally.
- Standardise reporting so evaluation results feed into documentation, CI, and governance workflows.
- Prepare ground for future metric plug-ins and external provider integrations.

## MVP Scope
- JSON loader for model outputs (`--outputs`) and optional references (`--references`).
- Default metrics:
  - Exact match (case-insensitive string comparison).
  - Toxicity keyword scan (simple lexical filter).
  - Length variance (difference between outputs and references).
- Report generation: structured JSON + Markdown summaries.
- CLI command `frai eval` wrapping the core harness.

## Data Expectations
- Outputs/reference files should be JSON arrays. Each element may be a string or object containing `text`/`output` fields.
- Future work: support tabular CSV, scored datasets, multi-turn conversations.

## Extensibility Hooks
- `frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js` exposes `DEFAULT_METRICS`; additional metrics can be registered by passing custom evaluators to `runEvaluations`.
- `writeReport` accepts `format` argument to enable additional exporters (HTML, CSV) later.
- CLI parsing accommodates further evaluation subcommands (e.g., `frai eval bias`).

## Follow-up Tasks
1. Integrate real toxicity/bias models once provider abstraction is implemented (Phase 0 → Providers milestone).
2. Extend datasets loader to support configurable schema mapping.
3. Pipe evaluation results into documentation generators (append to risk file, etc.).

## Thresholds for CI Gating

The CLI and SDK support optional thresholds to gate CI pipelines on metric scores:

### CLI Usage
```bash
frai eval --outputs outputs.json --threshold exact_match=0.9 --threshold toxicity=0.98
```

- Each `--threshold` takes the form `<metric_id>=<minimum_value>` (0–1 range).
- Valid metric IDs: `exact_match`, `toxicity`, `length_variance`, plus any custom metrics registered with an `id` field.
- Exit codes:
  - **0** if all thresholds pass (or no thresholds specified).
  - **1** if any threshold fails.
  - **2** if a threshold is malformed (not `metric=number`) or metric is unknown.
- Reports include `passed` (boolean) and `thresholds` array in JSON; Markdown reports add a "Thresholds" section.
- A metric with no score (e.g., `exact_match` when references are missing) fails its threshold.

### SDK Usage
```javascript
const report = Eval.generateReport({
  evaluations,
  outputsPath,
  referencesPath,
  thresholds: { exact_match: 0.9, toxicity: 0.98 }
});

if (report.passed === false) {
  // Handle threshold failure
}
```

The `thresholds` parameter is optional. Without it, reports have no `passed` or `thresholds` fields (backward compatible).

- `frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js` exposes `DEFAULT_METRICS`; additional metrics can be registered by passing custom evaluators to `runEvaluations`.
- Thresholds work with any metric that has an `id` field and a numeric `score` (or null).
